title: Deep threads stay readable: 'continue this thread →' pages beyond five levels, and a collapse/expand toggle on every comment
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

attempts.head: 203bba07ffa63917b4da83b06c1a2aa7713bded0
attempts.summary: Fixed the one defect the validation found: the scratch finish runner fell back to Chrome paths written in its own code when CHROME_BIN was unset.

caused_by.reason: validation partial this build: This stage only read the tree and the ledger, so its contact is `code`. Every product criterion of SC-013/SC-014 was verified, but the one failed defect check is real. It was waived only until a run showed it failing, and the validator's run has now shown that. What I checked myself: - **The defect is in the code.** `.taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py:29-30` defines `CHROME_PATHS` as the two Chrome paths under Program Files. `chrome()` at line 41 loops over `(os.environ.get("CHROME_BIN"), *CHROME_PATHS)`, so with CHROME_BIN unset it falls back to a browser path written into the code. The docstrings repeat the fallback: line 12 ("from CHROME_BIN or from the install paths"), line 39 ("CHROME_BIN, else an installed Chrome") and the line 49 message ("no Chrome is installed at the usual paths"). The file is tracked and was added in 78c9ccc, the build commit. - **The ledger rows.** I read them in place (`mode=ro`, SELECT only). - Decision 14105 (finding-triage, accepted-pending) confirmed code-review m3. It says the machine's CHROME_BIN-only rule outranks the earlier m5 wording ("CHROME_BIN and the Chrome install paths only"), so no person needs to decide between them. - Decision 14110 waived O-014 to N-071 only because the code review gave no reproduction. It says the item "becomes work when a run shows it failing". - The validator then reproduced it: with CHROME_BIN removed, importing the runner and calling `chrome()` returned `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`. That meets the waiver's own condition, and N-071 is still open. - **The fix will not break later runs.** CHROME_BIN is set in this environment and points at an existing chrome.exe, so a runner that reads only CHROME_BIN still runs the finish line and the look. - **I did not re-run anything.** The product evidence (the probe, the mutations, the 13 named tests, the Chrome look at 360/400/1000 px) is the validator's, and I accepted it as reported. What the builder must change, in `.taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py` only: 1. Delete `CHROME_PATHS`. 2. Make `chrome()` read only `os.environ.get("CHROME_BIN")`. 3. Keep refusing any basename that starts with msedge. 4. When CHROME_BIN is unset, empty, not a file, or Edge, print a message saying so on stderr and exit 3. It must never exit 0 and never 1. 5. Rewrite the module docstring (lines 5 and 12), the `chrome()` docstring and the line 49 message so they describe CHROME_BIN-only behaviour, with no mention of install paths. 6. Keep everything else as it is: the read-only ledger SELECT, the ROOT and browser-list patches that must each match exactly once (exit 4 otherwise), the assertion that no msedge text is left, and the look and serve modes. How to show it is fixed: - With CHROME_BIN removed from the environment, `python -I -X utf8 .taad/slices/SL-008/run_finish_e004_2.py --root <worktree>` exits 3 without starting a browser. - With CHROME_BIN pointing at an msedge.exe, it also exits 3. - With CHROME_BIN pointing at the installed chrome.exe, finish line 2 exits 0 and the Edge process count is the same before and after. Not part of this rebuild: - `internal/testutil/headless/headless.go:44-45`. Its Chrome default was decided in SL-004 and pinned by lesson #946. - The approved ledger finish body that still lists msedge. It was already reported to the person. - The stray tracked `__pycache__` .pyc. That is an extra and is carried, though the builder should not commit a regenerated one. - The waived N-066, N-067, N-069 and N-070.
